title: Flex sizing, grow, shrink, basis
learningObjectives: Explain flex sizing, grow, shrink, basis and build a responsive layout with it.

understand.concept: The flex shorthand combines flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis. Grow distributes positive free space, shrink helps items fit when space is insufficient, and basis provides the initial main size before free-space distribution.
understand.whyItMatters: Flex items have automatic minimum-size behaviour that can prevent shrinking around long content. min-width:0 or min-height:0 may be needed in some layouts, but content should still remain accessible.
understand.analogy: Flex sizing is like sharing seats: grow allocates spare seats, shrink handles a crowded row, and basis is each person's starting request.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual layout follows the flex or grid formatting algorithm.

explain.narrative: The first item keeps a seven-rem basis; the other two share remaining space and can shrink when needed.

examples.explanation: The first item keeps a seven-rem basis; the other two share remaining space and can shrink when needed.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered layout demonstrating the lesson concept.

practise.guidedTask: Change flex-grow and flex-shrink values. Add long unbroken text and test whether min-width:0 changes the result.
practise.independentTask: Build a small responsive interface using the concept. Test long labels and more than one viewport width.
hints: Inspect the layout overlay in developer tools.
Change one container or item property at a time.
Check for overflow and preserve reading order.

questions.prompt: Which flex factor distributes positive free space?
questions.explanation: flex-grow controls how an item receives positive free space.
